headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Kestra can move sensitive workflow data into RD-Agent’s API-backed research pipeline by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kestra can read/write files, ingest logs, messages, and workflow artifacts, while RD-Agent reads files and uses browser/API-driven research. If Kestra passes untrusted content into RD-Agent’s prompts or files, instruction-like payloads could be interpreted. The pairwise bridge is plausible but not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF Kestra exports workflow artifacts or logs into RD-Agent inputs without sanitization
IF RD-Agent treats retrieved papers, traces, or files as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Add a strict content separator and prompt-injection filter before handoff
Pass only allowlisted fields, not raw logs or artifacts
Review one sample handoff for instruction-like text
Disable automatic ingestion of free-form files into RD-Agent
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging across the handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kestra touches logs, inputs, variables, artifacts, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, and has broad network egress. RD-Agent sends context to OpenAI/Azure OpenAI/DeepSeek/LiteLLM and handles API keys. If Kestra forwards sensitive workflow data into RD-Agent, that data can leave the environment through third-party APIs. The interaction is not directly evidenced, but the default egress path makes leakage materially plausible.
conditions: IF Kestra workflow inputs include secrets, database data, or cloud storage data
IF RD-Agent is configured to call external LLM APIs on those inputs
mitigations: Remove secrets from the Kestra-to-RD-Agent handoff
Use a local-only model path for the research step
Rotate any API keys exposed to the shared workflow
Inspect one run for outbound payload contents
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction before API calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Kestra has filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and broad network egress; RD-Agent also has broad network egress and browser execution. Both support multiple instances, so concurrent writes or shared mutable resources can conflict if they target the same workspace or external account. Because no locking or shared-state controls are documented, uncertainty favors the higher severity.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, git repo, or database
IF both agents mutate the same external API quota or shared cloud resource
mitigations: Separate working directories per agent
Run only one writer at a time
Use per-agent credentials and quotas
Check for overlapping file paths before execution
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra can emit workflow outputs, logs, and notifications that RD-Agent may consume as research inputs. RD-Agent then uses those inputs to generate API-backed outputs. If RD-Agent treats Kestra-produced artifacts as authoritative, an upstream mistake can cascade into downstream analysis or actions. The pairwise pathway exists, but there is no direct evidence of automatic action-taking, so medium fits.
conditions: IF RD-Agent consumes Kestra logs, artifacts, or messages without verification
IF downstream reports or decisions are generated from that unverified input
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between agents
Require source citations for any Kestra-derived claim
Compare one RD-Agent output against the original Kestra artifact
Mark Kestra outputs as untrusted by default
requires-engineering: add validation rules before downstream action

E_compliance.rationale: Kestra handles workflow definitions, logs, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, while RD-Agent handles financial reports, competition datasets, execution traces, and logs. If regulated or sensitive data flows from Kestra into RD-Agent’s external API calls, retention and residency obligations can diverge. No explicit residency or certification data is provided, so this is a compliance-risk inference rather than a documented violation.
conditions: IF Kestra processes regulated workflow data that is forwarded to RD-Agent
IF RD-Agent sends that data to a third-party API without a matching DPA or retention policy
mitigations: Classify data before handoff
Block regulated data from the research pipeline
Review vendor terms for the API path
Set short retention on logs containing shared data
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
